reason.description: With `needs_input`, the blocker to resolve first. `sign_in` is a sign-in or account credentials. `verification_code` is a one-time code, a two-factor prompt or an email or text confirmation, including one sent during checkout. `payment` is payment details, a payment method or a wallet limit only the user can get around; a checkout specialist also uses it when a wallet refusal leaves the replacement payment choice to Muse. `approval` is permission for a commitment your assignment does not cover, such as sending, submitting, booking or cancelling something the user did not ask for; purchases are approved in the payment approval. `missing_information` is a fact you lack, such as an address, dates or account details. `decision` is a choice between options you found. `captcha` is a puzzle the bot-check specialist could not solve, only when your assignment says the user can take over this browser and no other site will do. `other` is none of these. Any other bot check or a site refusing access is never `needs_input`: the bot-check specialist works through it, and a block that remains is `blocked`, naming the site. With `blocked`, what ended the work; a blocked report always names one. `bot_wall` is a block page from bot detection that did not clear. `captcha_unsolved` is a puzzle the bot-check specialist could not solve. `ai_agent_refused` is a site that does not allow AI agents. `ip_blocked` is a block the page attributes to the network. `rate_limited` is a request limit or cooldown the page states in words. `sign_in_required` is a page that needs a sign-in. `sign_in_rejected` is a sign-in the site refused. `not_available` is something the site does not offer, such as an item, a date or a service. `site_error` is the site failing on its own side. `site_unreachable` is a site that does not load. `approval_denied` is an approval the user or policy refused. `browser_failure` is the browser failing, including a tool that did not work on the page. `order_unconfirmed` is an order or booking whose merchant outcome remains unresolved after all permitted verification, with no user input needed. Omit it for `completed`.
